items.title: 68533_Sam Jones oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee (Sam Jones) does not speak in the provided transcript; the mention of Leonard Feather is made solely by the Interviewer.

ctx.x: Miles plays less notes. Dizzy plays a lot of notes, you see. So that's the way it's different between and so the people they compared, they never thought and sat down and said what you say. These guys, it's fantastic, both of them so how can you compare them. Because they both is giants you know.

Well Leonard Feather admitted to me that the whole concept of the polls in jazz was something that he instigated because when he first came to this country, he was very drugged that here was the music that he had been listening to up in England and he was very excited about it and he came over, basically came over as a band boy with Duke Ellington and he couldn't understand why there was nothing really being written about the black jazz artist and he said that he wanted to see them get more visibility so he went…

they wanted to write about Red Nichols and some of them old, Jimmy Dorsey and people like that. They didn't want to write about these black jazz artists. And he said that the reason why he got the idea started was because of that reason, because it offered a thing that the magazine could relate to to stimulate their sales. But then the whole thing just got turned around, you know.
